models.name: Implant-Only Explicit Contact Model (IO-ECM)
models.what_it_computes: Transient tibiofemoral and patellofemoral contact pressures, contact areas, slip distances, plastic strain risk in the UHMWPE, and cumulative wear depth/volume using a pressure–sliding-distance wear formulation.

models.name: Joint-Integrated Explicit Model with Soft Tissues (JI-EM)
models.what_it_computes: Coupled tibiofemoral and patellofemoral mechanics with tension-only ligament bundles (MCL, LCL, capsule) and compliant extensor mechanism; predicts contact pressure distributions, kinematic constraints, insert micromotion, and cycle-integrated wear.

mechanisms.name: Load-controlled gait contact mechanics (ISO-style profiles)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Peak and average contact pressures during walking correlate with insert durability and backside micromotion risk.

mechanisms.name: UHMWPE wear accumulation over multi-million cycles
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Gravimetric wear rate and depth distribution drive debris generation and long-term insert survivorship.

mechanisms.name: Edge loading under tibial varus malalignment
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Malalignment concentrates stress near the insert rim, elevating damage and instability risk.

mechanisms.name: Patellofemoral contact in deep flexion tasks
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High patellofemoral pressures are linked to anterior knee pain and accelerated wear of the trochlear region of the insert.

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is scored on a 0–7 Credibility Index with 0.5 increments for every model × mechanism pair; matrices report per-factor medians and interquartile ranges on this scale.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Evidence spanning algorithmic verification, solver diagnostics bench comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and uncertainty propagation supported moderate-to-high credibility for both models in their intended uses, with the joint-integrated model earning higher levels where ligament and extensor behavior shape contact and wear.

findings.mechanism: Load-controlled gait contact mechanics (ISO-style profiles)
spans: Runs with reduced time steps (20% lower) changed peak contact pressures by less than 0.6% and contact areas by less than 1.2%, indicating numerical stability and minimal integration error contribution.

findings.mechanism: Load-controlled gait contact mechanics (ISO-style profiles)
spans: For the IO-ECM under gait, varying µ from 0.02 to 0.08 altered mid-stance peak pressure by ±6% and contact area by ±4%; changing UHMWPE yield onset ±2 MPa changed peak pressure by ±3%.

For IO-ECM gait, first-order indices for peak pressure ranked as: condylar radius (0.26), friction coefficient (0.17), UHMWPE yield onset (0.12), and axial load scaling (0.08), with total-order indices indicating limited interactions (<0.10 beyond the top two).
findings.span: For the IO-ECM under gait, varying µ from 0.02 to 0.08 altered mid-stance peak pressure by ±6% and contact area by ±4%; changing UHMWPE yield onset ±2 MPa changed peak pressure by ±3%.

findings.mechanism: Load-controlled gait contact mechanics (ISO-style profiles)
spans: For IO-ECM gait, the 95% predictive interval (PI) for peak tibiofemoral pressure was 16.9–21.1 MPa (width 4.2 MPa, approximately 23% of the mean), and contact area PI was 195–243 mm^2 (width 48 mm^2).
findings.span: For IO-ECM gait, the 95% predictive interval (PI) for peak tibiofemoral pressure was 16.9–21.1 MPa (width 4.2 MPa, approximately 23% of the mean), and contact area PI was 195–243 mm^2 (width 48 mm^2).

findings.mechanism: Load-controlled gait contact mechanics (ISO-style profiles)
spans: Load and motion profiles for gait were derived from ISO 14243-1 waveforms and verified in-house on a six-degree-of-freedom knee rig.
Axial load ranged from 0.3 to 3.0 kN with phasing aligned to knee flexion–extension over a 1.0 s stride; tracking errors averaged 1.8% RMS (n = 10 cycles).
findings.span: Load and motion profiles for gait were derived from ISO 14243-1 waveforms and verified in-house on a six-degree-of-freedom knee rig.

findings.mechanism: UHMWPE wear accumulation over multi-million cycles
spans: For multi-million-cycle wear, both models integrate the same pressure–sliding-distance rule with a cross-shear term, as the primary objective is to estimate gravimetric wear rate and spatial pattern.
